Never enter a flowing streambed, never camp overnight in a streambed, and on flash-flood warning days (Meteorological Service / INPA) avoid the wadis of the Judean Desert, the Negev and the Arava.

Southbound in autumn (SOBO): the north is still dry and you reach the Negev after the heat breaks, but with short days and flash-flood risk. Most Israeli hikers choose northbound in spring.

The common interpretation: white = the snow of the Hermon (north), blue = the sea, orange = the Negev desert (south). The Trails Committee stresses that the colours have no official meaning beyond identifying the trail.
צפע ארץ-ישראלי בצפון ובמרכז (מרץ–נובמבר): Palestine viper in the north and centre (March–November) – don't turn over stones, wear high boots, use a headlamp at night; if bitten – call 101, no tourniquet. Scorpions in the Negev – shake out shoes and gear in the morning. Hyenas and jackals are usually not dangerous – keep food sealed. Ticks in spring – check daily.
בצפון ובמרכז: ברזיות ביישובים, בתי עלמין: In the north and centre: drinking fountains in localities, cemeteries, petrol stations, field schools (Hermon, Meron? – check), springs (Ein Tina, Ein Koren, Nahal Amud, Ein Hemed) – spring water must be purified/filtered (leptospirosis and bacteria). KKL-JNF overnight campsites (e.g. in the Carmel and the Shephelah) usually have no tap.

Booking a seat in advance is recommended (egged.co.il or the Egged app) – especially on Saturday nights and holidays.
רשות הטבע והגנים: 4–6 ליטר לאדם ליום לשת: Israel Nature and Parks Authority: 4–6 litres per person per day for drinking alone. SPNI: 3–4 litres per day in the north and centre, 5–6 litres in the south; hikers report 6–7 litres on a hot day in the Arava (including cooking). Recommended carrying capacity: 4–6 litres (up to 8–9 litres when setting out on two-day stretches without water).
שלג יורד כמעט מדי חורף בחרמון (מקטעי הפת: Snow falls almost every winter on the Hermon (the opening sections from the Hermon to Tel Hai; the Hermon site closes to hikers in snow) and sometimes on Mount Meron (1,200 m) and in Safed – usually December–February, for a few days. A SOBO hiker leaving in October avoids it; a NOBO hiker reaching Meron in April will almost never meet snow.
צפע ארץ-ישראלי (Daboia palaestinae) – ~9: Palestine viper (Daboia palaestinae) – ~90% of venomous bites in Israel; especially active March–November and on summer nights. In the north and centre. Don't turn over stones, don't reach into crevices, wear high boots, use a headlamp at night. If bitten: stay calm, immobilize, call 101 – no tourniquet, no sucking, no ice.
שבת: מכניסת שבת (ו' לפנות ערב) עד צאת הש: Shabbat: from the start of Shabbat (Friday towards evening) until it ends (Saturday night) – no public transport, supermarkets and grocery stores in Jewish localities are closed (kibbutz grocery stores are usually closed on Friday afternoon too). Druze villages (Isfiya, Daliyat al-Karmel, Majdal Shams) and Arab villages – open; petrol stations on main roads are open.
אין מסורת של 'חבילות דואר' כמו בארה\"ב –: There is no tradition of 'mail drops' as in the US – distances are short and there are supermarkets. You can send a parcel via Israel Post/couriers to a post office or to a trail angel in Arad/Mitzpe Ramon (by arrangement), or leave gear with a trail angel. A 'desert kit' (jerrycans, food for 10 days) is usually brought to Arad/Mitzpe Ramon by car before the trek.
קטעי החרמון–תל חי (38 ק\"מ, נפתחו 2023): The Hermon–Tel Hai sections (38 km, opened 2023) were closed during the war (2023–2025) and reopened gradually; the Hermon site reopened in March 2025. In October 2026 the route north of Kiryat Shmona was temporarily diverted (Tel Hai–Kfar Giladi bridge works). Before heading out: check SPNI and INPA updates and the Home Front Command app.

The typical number of caches between Arad and Eilat: 6–8 (shvil wiki: 'on average 7 caches').
אוקטובר 2023 – 2025: קטעי הצפון (חרמון,: October 2023 – 2025: the northern sections (Hermon, Tel Hai, Upper Galilee near the Lebanese border) and the Gaza border area (not on the route) were closed/restricted under Home Front Command guidelines; bus lines in the Upper Galilee (e.g. line 36 Kiryat Shmona–Dan–Snir) were cancelled 'until further notice'. Most 2024 hikers started/finished at Tel Hai or further south.
מדרום לערד ועד אילת (כ-350 ק\"מ): בין ער: From south of Arad to Eilat (about 350 km): between Arad and the Zin Works, around the Hava/Mador campsites (Sde Boker–Mitzpe Ramon), Gev Holit, and elsewhere – on average 6–8 caches. INPA campsites with a tap (Nekarot West, Barak, Tzihor, Beer Milhan, Raham-Etek, Shehoret, Yehoram, Gevanim, Hod Akev, Mitzpe Makhtesh) make things easier but are no substitute for a backup.
שטחי אש (שטחי אימונים של צה\"ל) מכסים כ-: Firing zones (IDF training areas) cover about 7,500 sq km of the Negev. SPNI's rule: 'Hiking in firing zones requires coordination, and is usually possible only on weekends'. Coordination is required on Shabbat and holidays too – 'weekends only' is not an exemption from coordination. Check on a trail map (Israel Hiking Map shows firing zones with red hatching) whether the section crosses a firing zone.
מלאכי שביל (Trail Angels): תושבים לאורך: Trail angels: residents along the trail who host hikers for the night, a shower, laundry and food free of charge (or for a token fee) and help with water caching and shuttles. It is customary to call a day or two in advance, arrive as clean as possible, and leave the place clean. The updated list in English – israeltrail.net; in Hebrew – the shvil wiki and the Facebook groups.
The Israel National Trail is a winter-spring and autumn trail. The two accepted windows: northbound (NOBO) – leaving Eilat from late January to mid-March and finishing on the Hermon in April–May; southbound (SOBO) – leaving the Hermon/Dan in October to early November and finishing in Eilat in December–January. Do not attempt a full thru-hike in summer (June–September): the Negev and the Arava are life-threatening in the heat.
להוריד מראש: שכבת מפה לא-מקוונת (Israel: Download in advance: an offline map layer (Israel Hiking Map with a subscription, or Amud Anan, or OsmAnd/Organic Maps with the Israel map + the trail GPX), the official GPX for each section from SPNI, and the coordinates file of the water caches. Battery: a 10,000–20,000mAh power bank, airplane mode during the day; no reception in parts of the craters and in the Arava. A paper map of the Negev as backup.
חגים: ראש השנה ויום כיפור (ספטמבר/אוקטוב: Holidays: Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur (September/October – on Yom Kippur there is no traffic at all), Sukkot (a week of holidays – overnight campsites crowded and firing zones sometimes open), Passover (April – a week; leavened products not sold in many supermarkets), Independence Day (May – crowds outdoors, barbecues), Shavuot, Lag BaOmer (Meron – hundreds of thousands, the section near the tomb of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is crowded/closed).
בודקים ב-Israel Hiking Map (שטחי אש בקוו: Check on Israel Hiking Map (firing zones in red hatching) and on the section page on the SPNI website. The rule: hiking in a firing zone requires coordination with the Command's coordination office (South: 08-9902926/8, about two weeks in advance), and is usually possible only on weekends and holidays. Main sections: Nahal Tzihor–Shizafon, Paran/Tzihor–Shittim, Neot Smadar–Shaharut. Do not stray from the markings; unexploded ordnance – don't touch, call 100.
לפי רשות הטבע והגנים (parks.org.il/new/s: According to the Israel Nature and Parks Authority (parks.org.il/new/shvil-israel), overnight campsites with a drinking water supply in the southern part: Yehoram, Shehoret, Raham-Etek, Beer Milhan, Nahal Tzihor, Nahal Barak, Nekarot West, Nahal Gevanim, Hod Akev, Mitzpe Makhtesh (near Mitzpe Ramon). Open free of charge and without coordination; the water is for drinking only (not for showering/laundry). The taps are sometimes shut off – do not rely on a single tap without a backup.
מקטעי הפתיחה (כניסת אתר החרמון – נווה אט: The opening sections (Hermon site entrance – Neve Ativ – Nimrod – Tel Hai, ~38 km, opened August 2023) pass close to fenced minefields (yellow fence/red sign – do not cross), through military areas and near the border. Snow and ice in winter; the Hermon site closes to visitors during storms. During the war (October 2023 – 2025) the area was closed to hikers; the Hermon site reopened in March 2025. Check Home Front Command/INPA notices before heading out.
כלל הכיוון (Wikivoyage ומדריכים): כשהפס: The direction rule (Wikivoyage and guidebooks): when the white stripe is on top/leading – you are heading north; when the orange stripe is on top/leading – you are heading south. That is: in a 'regular' horizontal blaze the white is on top and the orange at the bottom; when the blaze is tilted/painted so that the orange is at the front end, the direction is south (to Eilat). This is a field convention, not a binding rule – in practice the decision is made by map/GPS, and the blaze only confirms you are on the trail. Arrows/double blazes mark a turn.

נַחַל צִבְעוֹן (בערבית: ואדי צוביע; נקרא: Nahal Tzivon (Arabic: Wadi Subei'; also called Nahal Gurei HaArayot – Lion Cubs Stream) is an ephemeral stream located in the Upper Galilee and one of the tributaries of Nahal Dishon.
תל גּוֹדֵד הוא אתר ארכאולוגי באזור שפלת: Tel Goded is an archaeological site in the Judean Shephelah, which includes among other things remains from the biblical period and the Roman period, and hiding complexes from the time of Bar Kokhba.
חבל לכיש הוא גוש התיישבות בדרום, בין הרי: The Lachish Region is a settlement bloc in the south, between the Judean Hills to the east and Ashkelon to the west. At its centre is the city of Kiryat Gat. The region is named after the ancient city of Lachish.
בית אהרנסון הוא ביתה של משפחת אהרנסון במ: The Aaronsohn House is the home of the Aaronsohn family in the moshava of Zikhron Ya'akov, and has housed the NILI Museum since 1956. The house stands at 40 HaMeyasdim Street in Zikhron Ya'akov.
א-נבי יושע (בערבית: النبي يوشع) היה כפר: An-Nabi Yusha (Arabic: النبي يوشع) was a Shia Arab village in the Upper Galilee, with a mausoleum and a Muslim cemetery. Today the locality of Ramot Naftali stands on the site.
נַחַל פּוֹלֵג (בערבית: وادي الفالق; ואדי: Nahal Poleg (Arabic: وادي الفالق; Wadi al-Faliq; the dividing stream) is a stream draining an area in the Sharon region of Israel, flowing into the Mediterranean north of the Wingate Institute in the Netanya area.
הר שחורת הוא חלק מרכס הרי אילת, ונמצא בי: Mount Shehoret is part of the Eilat Mountains ridge, located between Nahal Shehoret and Nahal Roded. It is so named because of the black rocks in its lower part that border Nahal Shehoret, which runs at its foot.
הארבל הוא מצוּק הנמצא בצפון ישראל במזרח: The Arbel is a cliff in northern Israel in the eastern Lower Galilee, north-west of Tiberias and north of the Arbel Valley. Mount Arbel rises to 181 metres above sea level, about 390 metres above the Sea of Galilee.
שַׁחֲרוּת הוא יישוב קהילתי בערבה השייך ל: Shaharut is a community settlement in the Arava belonging to the Hevel Eilot Regional Council, about 37 km north of the city of Eilat. It is located on the edge of the fault escarpment, west of Kibbutz Yotvata, 550 metres above sea level.
נחל עַפְרָן (מערבית: وادي عفران, תעתיק מ: Nahal Afran (from Arabic: وادي عفران, exact transliteration: Wadi Afran) is an ephemeral stream on the southern slopes of the Hatira Ridge in the northern Negev. The stream has a steep canyon channel with waterfalls, rock pools and an impressive gorge.
רָמוֹת נַפְתָּלִי הוא מושב באזור הצפון ל: Ramot Naftali is a moshav in the Northern District near the border between Israel and Lebanon, belonging to the Mevo'ot HaHermon Regional Council. The locality is so named because it is located in the Naftali Hills, within the territory of the tribe of Naftali.
מצפה עופר הוא מצפה יערנים של קק\"ל, השוכ: Mitzpe Ofer is a KKL-JNF foresters' lookout located in the Hof HaCarmel Forest, on the western slopes of the Carmel, between the localities of Kerem Maharal to the east and Tzrufa to the west. The site is named after the nearby Moshav Ofer.
מנזר גְבירתנו של שבעת המכאובים, הידוע יו: The Monastery of Our Lady of the Seven Sorrows, better known as Latrun Monastery or the Monastery of the Silent Monks, is a Benedictine-Cistercian-Trappist monastery for men, located in Latrun at the south-eastern end of the Ayalon Valley.
Arad is a city in the Southern District of Israel. The city lies in the Judean Desert, on the Kidod Ridge, at an elevation of about 600 metres above sea level. Its municipal area is 125,610 dunams. Arad was declared a city in 1995.
יער לַהַב הוא יער נטוע בדרום ישראל הממוק: Lahav Forest is a planted forest in southern Israel located between the northern Negev, the southern Judean Shephelah and the southern Hebron Hills, covering about 30,000 dunams. The localities adjacent to it are Dvir, Lahav, Lehavim, Lakiya and Eshkolot.
תל לכיש (בערבית: تل الدوير, תל אֶ-דֻּוֵי: Tel Lachish (Arabic: تل الدوير, Tell ed-Duweir) is a major tell in the Judean Shephelah. It covers about 124 dunams and was identified by the American scholar William Albright in 1926. In 1994 it was declared a national park.
אַלּוֹנִים הוא קיבוץ בצפון עמק יזרעאל, ל: Alonim is a kibbutz in the northern Jezreel Valley, near Kiryat Tiv'on, affiliated with the Kibbutz Movement. The kibbutz, which settled at its present location in 1938, lies within the jurisdiction of the Jezreel Valley Regional Council.
נחל נקרות הוא נחל אכזב באזור מכתש רמון ה: Nahal Nekarot is an ephemeral stream in the Makhtesh Ramon area that flows into Nahal HaArava. In Arabic the stream is called Wadi al-Jarir ("the dragging stream"). It is so named because of the many niches carved by flash floods into the canyon walls.
פארק נחל חדרה הוא פארק שמנוהל על ידי נחל: Nahal Hadera Park is a park managed by Nehalim, the Hadera Tourism Development Company, located in the western part of Nahal Hadera, between Road 2 to the east and the Mediterranean coast to the west, and south of the Orot Rabin power station.
מְצָדָה (מַסָּדָה בכתיב מיושן) הוא מבצר: Masada (Metzada; 'Massada' in older spelling) is an ancient fortress on the summit of an isolated mesa on the eastern edge of the Judean Desert, rising to 63 metres above sea level and about 480 metres above the Dead Sea at its foot.
כעביה-טבאש-חג'אג'רה (בערבית: كعبية، طباش:
Ka'abiyye-Tabbash-Hajajre (Arabic: كعبية، طباش،حجاجرة) is a local council in the Northern District of Israel. It was declared a local council in 1996. 
The locality has a health clinic, a football pitch, a community centre and two mosques.
קִרְיַת שְׁמוֹנָה היא העיר הצפונית ביותר: Kiryat Shmona is the northernmost city in Israel. As the only city in the Galilee Panhandle, located alongside Road 90, Kiryat Shmona serves as a regional centre for the surrounding localities in health services, industry, business services and commerce.
נַחַל דִּישוֹן (בעבר ואדי חינדאג') הוא ה: Nahal Dishon (formerly Wadi Hindaj) is the largest of the streams of the eastern Upper Galilee. It begins on the eastern slopes of Mount Meron, is about 31 km long, and at its end flows into the Jordan River (formerly into Lake Hula), north of the Pkak Bridge.
חורבת עָנִים (במקור: ח'רבת ע'ווין א-תחתא: Horvat Anim (originally Khirbet Ghuwein at-Tahta) is the name of a site in the southern Hebron Hills containing the remains of a biblical and Talmudic settlement, about 20 km north-west of Arad and within Yatir Forest. The site is near the locality of Livne to the south-west.
תֵּל-חָדִיד הוא תל הנמצא מצָפון ליער בן: Tel Hadid is a tell located north of Ben Shemen Forest and Road 443 and south of Nahal Natuf. The tell sits on the first line of hills above the coastal plain in the Ben Shemen area and overlooks all of Gush Dan. The Israel National Trail, section no. 20, passes through Tel Hadid.
מרכז ג'ו אלון הוא מרכז חינוכי ותיירותי ל: The Joe Alon Center is an educational and tourism centre for the study of the land and the Negev, located on the edge of Lahav Forest in the northern Negev, just west of Kibbutz Lahav. The centre is best known for the Museum of Bedouin Culture housed there. The centre is named after the pilot Joe Alon.
עין נטפים (בערבית: ביר אל קטר או עין אל: Ein Netafim (Arabic: Bir al-Qatar or Ein al-Qatar) is a freshwater spring in the Eilat Mountains in the channel of Nahal Netafim near the border with Egypt. The spring is about seven km north of Eilat, near Road 12. It is the only spring that flows year-round in the area near Eilat.
סַנְסַנָּה היא התנחלות דתית במתכונת של י: Sansana is a religious settlement in the form of a community settlement in the Meitarim region on the border of the northern Negev and the Hebron Hills, located mostly east of the Green Line but west of the separation barrier, belonging to the Har Hevron Regional Council, where it is the westernmost locality, and to the Amana movement.
סיירת אגוז (נקראה גם גדוד 483) הוקמה לרא: Sayeret Egoz (also called Battalion 483) was first established in 1956 as the Northern Command's reconnaissance unit on the orders of the Northern Command's commanding general, Yitzhak Rabin, after Israel invaded Sinai during Operation "Kadesh". Its founder and first commander was Aryeh Gardi. The unit was disbanded in 1974.
כפר כַּנָּא (בערבית: كفر كنا) היא מועצה: Kafr Kanna (Arabic: كفر كنا) is an Arab local council in the Lower Galilee, located north of the cities of Nof HaGalil and Nazareth. It was declared a local council in 1968. About 90% of the village's residents are Muslim and the rest Christian. The locality is identified with the ancient settlement of Cana, sacred to Christianity.
אַפּוֹלוֹנְיָה־אַרְסוּף (גם תֵּל אַרְשָׁ: Apollonia-Arsuf (also Tel Arshaf) is an ancient fortress and city whose remains lie on the coastal plain on the kurkar cliffs of the southern Sharon, west of the Nof Yam neighbourhood in Herzliya, near present-day Sidna Ali. The site has been prepared for visitors and a national park was established there.
